newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-New retail jobs point to UK consumer boom.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-New retail jobs point to UK consumer boom.

text.p: Storehouse Plc on Thursday joined a growing list of retailers planning to expand and create new jobs, supporting the view that Britain's economy is booming.

But while shoppers are feeling more confident and willing to spend, retailers are still finding life extremely tough and their investment in expansion and staff represents an effort to buoy sales, analysts said.
Storehouse, owner of Mothercare and Bhs chains, is spending 120 million pounds ($197 million) to create 1,000 jobs and refurbish its 141 Bhs outlets.

Earlier this week retail sector leader Marks and Spencer Plc said it would take on about 1,700 new staff and add half a million square feet of new space in Britain this year. Last week Burton Group Plc unveiled plans to open nine more Debenhams department stores over the next four years, creating 3,400 jobs.

Industry analysts said this showed the retail economy had picked up and it was set to benefit further this year from the cash windfalls millions of people will receive from building society flotations - estimated around 20 billion pounds.
Many mutually owned home loan societies are seeking stock exchange listings to become fully operational as banks.
"It is picking up," said Richard Perks of Verdict Research. "There was a pause before the election when people held back, but we're optimistic for the rest of the year."
Other analysts agreed there was undoubtedly a "feel better factor", but said retailers were still facing a huge struggle to get consumers to part with their cash.
"It's still fiercely competitive, there's no room for margin expansion," said Rowan Morgan at Nikko Europe.
Profit forecasts for retailers this year have already been scaled back, because the current earnings and sales have not lived up to what were probably overblown expectations, analysts said.
"Despite the fact that we're in a consumer boom earnings forecasts are still coming down," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.
Argos Plc and Laura Ashley Holdings Plc have both issued profit warnings, M&S disappointed on its food sales and Burton's fashion chains performed less well than expected.
"The results season has mostly disappointed one way or another," said another analyst.

Earnings forecasts for Storehouse's current year were shaved after the group reported only modest increases in sales in the first eight weeks of its current year. Morgan at Nikko said he was cutting his to 128 million pounds from 132 million.
Analysts saw the investment in extra staff and refurbishment as a worrying trend pointing to higher costs.
"All of these chains are finding they actually have to invest either in refurbishment or new capacity or services to actually drive top line growth," said another analyst.
M&S has the sales to justify the investment, but for some of the others it was more of a worry, he said.
Other analysts believe the retail sector has passed its best point in terms of the cost cycle and upward pressure on wages and rents could emerge over the medium term.

Worries about rising interest rates and the possibility of tax hikes in next month's budget, the new Labour government's first, has also been weighing on sentiment for some time and the retail sector is still underperforming the equity market.
